channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Entre embate com Flávio Bolsonaro e memes, campanha de Lula vive disputa por influência no comando da estratégia digital
item.description: Lula’s 2026 campaign is experiencing an internal struggle over digital strategy: while Sidônio Palmeira, minister of Secom, advocates for an institutional and light approach focused on national pride and events like São João festivals, Nicole Briones and Ricardo Stuckert push for a more aggressive stance on social media, particularly in attacks against Flávio Bolsonaro, highlighting his ties to Daniel Vorcaro. Despite Sidônio’s influence, Lula’s personal Instagram account (14.7 million followers) will be managed by Briones and Stuckert, aligned with the PT’s goal to intensify digital confrontation.

item.title: Lula vai discutir valorização de países com terras-raras no G7
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will attend the G7 summit in France in June 2026 as a guest, focusing on the valorization of critical minerals, particularly rare earths, and balanced economic growth. Although Brazil is not a G7 member and will not participate in formal negotiations, Lula aims to endorse agreements aligned with Brazilian priorities, including international partnerships and child online protection, while avoiding discussions on U.S. tariffs and Middle East and Ukraine conflicts. The Brazilian delegation will only access final documents after approval by all G7 members.

item.title: O destino de Sidônio será definido em três semanas
item.description: Lula agreed with Sidônio Palmeira that, in the first week of July, the minister will decide whether to leave the government to fully dedicate himself to the electoral campaign or remain in the Palácio do Planalto until the first round of the election. The decision will be made within three weeks and will directly impact the PT's electoral strategy. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Com uso da máquina, Lula dribla a oposição, e Flávio precisará de um ‘rebranding’
item.description: Lula reversed negative perceptions of his government by implementing popular but costly measures like fuel price cuts and the repeal of the 'blusinha' tax, regaining control of the national debate. Flávio Bolsonaro suffers from a damaged image tied to alleged corruption with banker Daniel Vorcaro and accusations of prompting U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, requiring a rebranding effort to restore voter trust.

item.title: Ministra do TSE sinaliza análise rápida sobre ação de Flávio Bolsonaro contra pesquisa
item.description: Minister Estela Aranha of the TSE indicated she will conduct a rapid analysis before releasing the judgment on the AtlasIntel poll showing a drop for Flávio Bolsonaro, after requesting a view in Tuesday’s session. Kassio Nunes Marques’ decision to suspend the poll over alleged manipulation due to the display of a video of Bolsonaro’s conversation with banker Daniel Vorcaro was endorsed by the PL. The TSE is expected to resume the judgment following a meeting with polling institutes, scheduled for the coming days.

item.title: Prefeitura restringe acesso à lista de convidados ao camarote que recebeu Lula na Sapucaí
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro City Hall restricted access to the guest list for the municipal institutional box at Marquês de Sapucaí during the March samba school parades, which hosted President Lula and First Lady Janja da Silva. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Más notícias para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: President Lula saw modest improvements in overall government approval and specific policies according to the Genial/Quaest poll, while Senator Flávio Bolsonaro faced negative evaluations of his actions, statements, and electoral strategy. His conversation with Daniel Vorcaro, funding of the film 'Dark Horse', and reliance on U.S. government support in his campaign were particularly criticized, with 47% agreeing with Lula that Bolsonaro sought new tariffs harmful to Brazilian businesses.

item.title: Flávio retrocede
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian election is being shaped by 'swing voters' — independent electors who shift their support based on perceptions of corruption and fears about party continuity or ascension to power. Currently, the prospect of Lula seeking a fourth term or Bolsonaro’s return via his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, is driving these volatile voter behaviors. The subscriber-only article emphasizes that these shifts are not ideological but pragmatic, driven by institutional anxieties and governance concerns.

item.title: GP Brasil, feira de vinil, festas para os solteiros: os eventos no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's event agenda from June 11–17 features the 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix, singles parties, vinyl fairs and cultural attractions. The GP Brasil 2026 celebrates the centenary of the Gávea Hippodrome with turf races, a gastronomic fair and children's activities. Other highlights include the Vinyl Fair with 60 exhibitors, the National Festival of Popular and Solidarity Economy at Píer Mauá, and musical events such as the talk between Zé Pedro and Joanna at Blue Note.

item.title: PT pede que STF e PF investiguem se houve 'caixa 2' para campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro no filme Dark Horse
item.description: The PT filed a request with the STF and PF to investigate alleged 'caixa 2' illicit financing in Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, claiming funds from the film 'Dark Horse' were used to support Eduardo Bolsonaro's political structure in the U.S. The party cites Intercept Brasil reports linking Flávio Bolsonaro to Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master and questions the use of parliamentary amendments, Ancine registrations, and foreign actors' work visas.

item.title: A conta no longo prazo: especialistas alertam para o impacto fiscal das ‘pautas-bomba’ aprovadas no Senado
item.description: The Senate approved three proposals labeled 'bombshell agendas' by the Lula government, despite Executive appeals to block them. The most impactful is the rural debt renegotiation, which advanced after senators and the economic team failed to reach an agreement. The measures carry billion-dollar costs and raise concerns about long-term fiscal impact.

item.title: O eleitor que tapa o nariz
item.description: The independent voter, exemplified by Seu Valdir, is decisive in the 2026 elections, rejecting both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro due to distrust, not hatred. The anti-corruption banner lost its Bolsonarist appeal as voters perceive suspicion on both sides, while the defense of Brazil’s interests now favors Lula among independents. This volatile, distrust-driven vote prevents premature celebration by any campaign.

item.title: Peça-chave para outubro, eleitores 'independentes' ajudam Lula a recuperar vantagem sobre Flávio
item.description: Genial/Quaest poll shows President Lula regained lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro following scandals involving audio recordings in which the senator asked a banker for money to finance a film and new episodes linked to the United States. Lula opened a ten-point lead in the first round and six points in the second round. The survey was conducted after the audio leak and new controversies involving the senator.

item.title: Após ação do PSD, candidato do Novo ao governo do Rio nega uso de IA em locução e diz ter feito 'sátira política'
item.description: André Marinho, Novo party candidate for Rio governor, denied using AI in voiceovers of videos critical of Eduardo Paes, stating the voice is his own and the content is political satire. The PSD filed with TRE-RJ alleging illegal advance negative propaganda and electoral defamation, citing lack of AI disclosure as required by TSE. Marinho trusts electoral justice will distinguish satire from misconduct.

item.title: 10 pontos da Quaest, que mostra Lula ampliar vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro após caso Master
item.description: The June Quaest poll shows President Lula extending his lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to six points in a simulated runoff, with 44% to 38%. This shift follows the release of audio recordings involving Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro regarding funding for the film 'Dark Horse', which damaged the senator’s image. Among independent voters, Lula rose from 29% to 37%, while Flávio dropped from 31% to 24%.

item.title: Diplomatas apostam em encontro de Lula com Trump no G7 para evitar novas tarifas dos EUA contra o Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian government is betting on a meeting between Lula and Trump at the G7 in France to avert new U.S. tariffs, which Brasília views as politically driven and ignoring technical arguments already presented. Though not a G7 member, Lula was invited by host Macron, and diplomats believe a direct presidential meeting could break the technical negotiation deadlock at the USTR. Brazil has already responded with the Reciprocity Law, passed by Congress with government support, to retaliate against unilateral U.S. measures.

item.title: “Nós estamos preparados antecipadamente”, diz Lula sobre El Niño
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil is proactively prepared to face the impacts of the upcoming El Niño, emphasizing preventive actions against wildfires and climate disasters. He announced an environmental package including R$2 billion for Ibama and ICMBio, creation of national parks, regulation of the National Environment Fund and the National Policy for Payment for Environmental Services, as well as the establishment of Sintrilhas and APBio.

item.title: Los presidentes Lula y Sheinbaum reafirman juntos su defensa de la no injerencia en plena presión de Trump en Colombia y Cuba
item.description: Presidents Lula and Sheinbaum reaffirmed in a videoconference their commitment to multilateralism, international law, democracy, and the principle of non-interference, amid external pressures. The meeting between the leaders of Latin America’s two largest economies underscored their joint defense of national sovereignty in a complex global context.

item.title: Kassio usa adiamento no TSE para tentar acordo sobre pesquisas e evitar desgaste por censura
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques aims to use the postponement of the ruling on the censorship of the Atlas/Bloomberg poll to negotiate an agreement with other justices and reduce the political fallout from the provisional decision that blocked the release of the survey showing a decline in Flávio Bolsonaro's support.

item.title: Ministro do TSE advoga para big tech no STF em ação sobre Marco Civil da Internet
item.description: TSE Minister Floriano de Azevedo Marques also acts as counsel for Google in the STF regarding the Marco Civil da Internet case, where the court expanded digital platforms' duties and responsibilities. This dual role raises concerns about potential conflicts of interest between his electoral authority duties and his legal advocacy for major tech firms.

item.title: PT pede a Dino que investigue financiamento de filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: The PT urged Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino to investigate the funding of the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays Jair Bolsonaro's political trajectory, citing evidence of possible misappropriation of parliamentary amendments and economic power abuse. The party alleges that Flávio Bolsonaro personally influenced the release of funds and links the project to pre-candidacies of other Bolsonaro family members, forming a 'benefited political group'.

item.title: Moraes autoriza visita de Flávio, netas e nora de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes authorized a visit for Jair Bolsonaro’s son Flávio Bolsonaro, daughter-in-law Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, and two minor granddaughters while the former president serves house arrest since March 24. The visit, scheduled for Saturday, 13, from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m., is deemed compatible with the purposes of house arrest, aiming to preserve essential family support during his sentence, with visitors subject to search and electronic devices held by police.

item.title: Conselhão recomenda que Lula encerre subsídios a combustíveis fósseis
item.description: The Economic and Social Development Council (Conselhão) recommended that President Lula phase out fossil fuel subsidies, redirecting saved resources toward clean energy and compensatory social policies. The proposal aims to correct price distortions, fiscal dependence, and delays in decarbonization, aligning with the global pathway developed for COP30. The report acknowledges resistance from fossil fuel-linked groups, advocating for a gradual and just transition.

item.title: Michelle diz que Bolsonaro piorou e teve tratamento reformulado
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro stated that ex-president Jair Bolsonaro experienced a health deterioration, interrupting a three-day medication taper, and required a treatment reformulation by Dr. Brasil Caiado. She noted a temporary improvement on the afternoon of June 9, followed by a relapse, with Bolsonaro currently under home medical care and awaiting tests. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year and 3-month sentence for attempted coup d'état, under temporary house arrest due to his health condition.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: pesquisa mostra mudança em grupo decisivo para eleição de 2026
item.description: The Quaest poll reveals that the decisive group for the 2026 election are independent voters, representing about 30% of the electorate and more sensitive to shifts in economic and political conditions. Their recent shift in favor of Lula explains his improved performance in recent polls, after previously leaning toward Flávio Bolsonaro. Independents, lacking strong ideological identification, tend to react more quickly to news events and economic changes.

item.title: Lula sugere que terras demarcadas sejam usadas para turismo
item.description: President Lula suggested that demarcated indigenous lands and forest reserves be used to promote sustainable tourism in Brazil, arguing these protected areas can generate revenue for conservation and benefit local communities. He announced a package of environmental investments, including R$ 834 million from the Climate Fund, R$ 393 million for the Restaura Amazônia initiative, R$ 370 million to the Arpa Communities program, and R$ 270 million from the UK to the Amazon Fund, plus the launch of the Recaatingar Program with an initial R$ 60 million contribution. Lula emphasized that expanding visitation in protected areas can strengthen environmental awareness, create income, and boost societal support for conservation policies.

item.title: Os dois fatores que pesaram contra Flávio Bolsonaro na nova pesquisa Quaest sobre eleição presidencial
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll found that Flávio Bolsonaro lost electoral potential due to his rapprochement with Daniel Vorcaro for funding the film 'Dark Horse' and his actions alongside the U.S. government, particularly in pushing to label PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist groups. Although 65% of voters believe he erred in seeking Vorcaro's support, 76% say it won’t change their vote. His damaged image helps explain Lula’s lead in the polls.

item.title: Lula e Sheinbaum discutem comércio e parceria entre Petrobras e Pemex
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum discussed bilateral trade and a potential agreement between Petrobras and Pemex during a videoconference on June 10, 2026. They also reaffirmed support for ending the U.S. embargo on Cuba, endorsed Michelle Bachelet’s candidacy for UN Secretary-General, and wished Mexico success in hosting the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which opened on June 11. The call included Foreign Ministers Mauro Vieira and Roberto Velasco and emphasized energy cooperation, biofuels, and updating the bilateral commercial framework.

item.title: Lula diz que empresários “aprenderam” a respeitar acordos ambientais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazilian business leaders have learned to respect environmental agreements, recognizing that non-compliance leads to economic losses and hinders product commercialization. He emphasized the productive sector's evolution toward sustainable practices and said Brazil has regained international environmental credibility due to the efforts of environmentalists, regulatory agencies, and former Environment Minister Marina Silva.

item.title: O dado das pesquisas que pode acender alerta para Lula mesmo com queda de Flávio
item.description: The decline of Flávio Bolsonaro in 2026 election polls did not translate into electoral gains for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, whose support levels remained stable. According to Murilo Hidalgo of Paraná Pesquisas, the votes lost by Flávio were captured by other center-right candidates, including Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, and Joaquim Barbosa, showing that Lula failed to expand his base despite the senator's setbacks.

item.title: Governo amplia proteção ambiental e prepara recuperação de florestas
item.description: President Lula announced a package of environmental measures on World Environment Day, including the creation of new conservation units, expansion of protected areas, enactment of the National Policy for Caatinga Recovery, and streamlining of the National Environment Fund transfers to states and municipalities for wildfire prevention. He noted Brazil recorded less than 1 million hectares of deforestation in 2025 (984,700 ha) — an unprecedented feat — and said the country is now proactively prepared to face extreme climate events like El Niño.

item.title: Alvos de medidas de Trump, presidentes de Brasil e México reiteram defesa da não interferência estrangeira
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum reaffirmed their commitment to multilateralism, international law, and non-interference in a videoconference amid new U.S. tariff threats against Brazil and Mexico. They also voiced support for ending the U.S. embargo on Cuba, backing Michelle Bachelet’s bid for UN Secretary-General, and advancing the VI Binational Mexico-Brazil Commission. The discussion took place as the USTR recommended tariffs on Brazil over alleged unfair practices involving PIX, ethanol, anti-deforestation policies, and intellectual property.

item.title: Marco Civil da Internet: Toffoli começa a votar nos embargos e traz mudanças na tese
item.description: Justice Dias Toffoli, rapporteur of the STF in the judgment of the embargos against the Marco Civil da Internet, introduced innovations in his partial vote, maintaining subjective liability of platforms for third-party content, except in marketplaces where objective CDC liability applies. He proposes to further mitigate the application of Article 19, making liability dependent on the level of platform interference in content circulation, with neutral providers (like Wikipedia) requiring judicial decision to be held liable. Toffoli also suggested a 60-day adaptation period for big techs and that the new thesis apply only to actions filed after the publication of the judgment's record.

item.title: Governo avalia ir ao STF contra pauta-bomba de R$ 140 bi
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the Senate-approved rural debt renegotiation project could cost the National Treasury R$140 billion in the coming years, exceeding the government's fiscal capacity. He said the government will seek amendments in the Chamber of Deputees, may recommend presidential vetoes, and could challenge the project in the Supreme Federal Court if it violates the Fiscal Responsibility Law.

item.title: “Crime de adulto, pena de adulto”, diz Zema
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) celebrated the approval of PEC 32/2015 by the Chamber's Constitution and Justice Committee, which lowers the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16 for serious crimes. In a post on X, he defended the measure with the phrase 'Crime of adulthood, punishment of adulthood'.

item.title: Diante de pesquisas desfavoráveis, oposição a Lula ainda debate o que fazer
item.description: The opposition to Lula struggles with strategic shortcomings by over-relying on opinion polls, leading to candidate choices like Flávio Bolsonaro driven more by anti-Lula sentiment than substantive platforms. This short-term focus leaves center-right groups exposed when polls shift, especially in a volatile environment where external factors such as inflation and high interest rates could undermine the incumbent regardless of the challenger.

item.title: Lula abre seis pontos de vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno, indica Quaest
item.description: Lula leads a potential runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro with 44% voting intention, compared to 38% for the PL senator, according to the Genial/Quaest poll. The six-point advantage reflects a consolidation of support for the president in a polarized scenario. The poll was reported by O Antagonista.

item.title: Veto da UE à carne brasileira foi por falha de ministério, diz Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, former governor of Goiás and pre-candidate for president from the PSD, blamed the Ministry of Agriculture for bureaucratic failure in clearing Brazilian beef exports to the European Union, which led to a ban effective September 3, impacting over R$9 billion in Brazilian agribusiness. He attended a meeting at the EU Delegation in Brasília with Senator Nelsinho Trad and PSD national president Gilberto Kassab, urging the EU to reconsider restrictions that prohibit antimicrobial use for growth promotion in livestock. Caiado advocated for an international perspective, arguing that domestic issues should not be solved by penalizing other nations, and noted that other Mercosul countries remain authorized to export beef to the EU.

item.title: Senado aprova pauta-bomba que custará R$ 140 bi aos cofres públicos
item.description: The Senate symbolically approved Bill 5.122/2023, authorizing the use of R$ 140 billion from the Pre-Salt Social Fund and other surpluses to renegotiate rural debts of producers affected by climate and geopolitical events. While Finance Minister Dario Durigan defended the measure as necessary to support the agribusiness sector, critics warn it risks public finances amid global uncertainty. The bill returns to the Chamber of Deputies after Senate amendments.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa deve quebrar silêncio sobre pré-candidatura na próxima semana, diz presidente do DC
item.description: The president of the Christian Democracy party, João Caldas, states that Joaquim Barbosa's pre-candidacy for president will prosper, despite the former STF minister's current silence. Caldas expects Barbosa to begin speaking with the press next week and then take to the streets to launch his campaign. However, polls show Barbosa has only 1% of national voting intentions, with limited support concentrated in the Southeast (2%) and negligible presence in the South and Northeast.

item.title: Nunes Marques vota por manter pesquisa suspensa, mas pedido de vista adia decisão no TSE
item.description: The judgment on the release of the AtlasIntel presidential poll was interrupted at the TSE after rapporteur Minister Kassio Nunes Marques voted to maintain the suspension of the survey. A request for vista delayed the final plenary decision, keeping the poll suspended for now.

item.title: Durigan diz que governo avalia vetar renegociação de dívidas rurais caso projeto passe na Câmara; Senado aprovou proposta
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the government is considering a veto or STF action if the rural debt renegotiation bill passes the Chamber, after the Senate approved it with amendments. Dubbed a 'budget bomb,' the measure could cost between R$120 billion and R$140 billion, increasing public debt. Despite government opposition, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre brought it to vote without executive support.

item.title: Como está a disputa entre Keiko Fujimori e Sánchez entre peruanos de 11 capitais brasileiras
item.description: In Peru's presidential runoff, Roberto Sánchez (left) leads nationally with 50,03% of the vote against Keiko Fujimori (right) at 49,97%, with 97.9% of ballots counted. However, among Peruvians residing in Brazil, Fujimori leads with 55.7% of the vote across 11 state capitals, winning in nine of them, including São Paulo, where the race remains tight at 50.8% to 49.2%.

item.title: Senado aprova 'pauta-bomba' e negociação de dívidas rurais avança no Congresso; Fazenda calcula impacto de R$ 140 bilhões
item.description: The Senate approved a bill allowing rural producers to renegotiate their debts, expanding the scope beyond its original focus on those affected by public calamities. The Lula government opposes the measure, with the Ministry of Finance estimating a fiscal impact of R$ 140 billion by 2027, and had sought to block it but failed to reach an agreement with senators. The bill, already passed by the Chamber of Deputies, must now return for a new vote due to Senate amendments, leaving room for future negotiations or a provisional measure.

item.title: Senado aprova renegociação de dívidas de produtores rurais; governo é contra e vê projeto como pauta-bomba
item.description: The Senate approved a bill to renegotiate rural debts for producers affected by extreme weather and international geopolitical conflicts, despite opposition from the Lula government, which estimates a fiscal impact of up to R$ 140 billion. Senate rapporteur Renan Calheiros claims the cost will be lower, around R$ 120 billion over ten years, limited to overdue debts. The bill must return to the Chamber of Deputies for a new vote before presidential sanction.

item.title: Senado apresenta sua TV 3.0 em encontro de emissoras da Rede Legislativa
item.description: The Senate officially launched its TV 3.0 during the Legislative Network Radio and TV Meeting 2026 in Brasília, emphasizing the integration of open broadcast and streaming on a single device. Developed for over a year, the technology aims to expand the reach of legislative broadcasters, including in areas without open signal, and strengthen public communication as a tool for promoting citizenship and democracy, particularly ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Renan Santos descarta aliança com Aécio: “Não faz sentido”
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for the Presidency of the Republic, ruled out an alliance with Aécio Neves, federal deputy and national president of the PSDB, stating that such a partnership "does not make sense." He avoided elaborating but suggested the answer would be "crude" if pressed further. The statement was made on Wednesday, the 10th, and attracted media attention.

item.title: Após queda em pesquisas, Flávio vai visitar Bolsonaro neste sábado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) will visit former President Jair Bolsonaro this Saturday, following authorization from Minister Alexandre de Moraes, amid declining poll numbers. A Quaest poll shows he is six points behind Lula in a potential runoff, with 38% versus Lula’s 44%. The visit comes after a scandal involving an alleged request for funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro to produce a biopic about Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Fachin critica tentativas de questionar atos de autoridades brasileiras no exterior e faz alerta sobre ingerência
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin warned against efforts to challenge acts of Brazilian authorities in foreign tribunals, stating such actions may produce cross-border consequences and defending respect for national institutional independence. He stressed that cooperation between democracies does not justify interference in sovereign internal affairs and linked judicial independence to the protection of constitutional democracy.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Senado inspeciona códigos-fonte dos sistemas eleitorais no TSE
item.description: The Federal Senate inspected the source code of the electoral systems used by the TSE in Brasília as part of the Democratic Transparency Cycle. The verification, held on Wednesday (10), included opening an electronic voting machine to demonstrate its internal operation and presenting the software by Rodrigo Coimbra, head of the TSE’s Electronic Voting Section, who emphasized the system’s security, transparency, and auditability. União Brasil had conducted the first inspection in May.
